assets.credit: Cocharelli, Italian bankers, c. 1340. Public domain.
assets.depicts: Illustrative: a 14th-century Genoese manuscript painting of bankers at their counting table (the banca); not a bankruptcy.

assets.credit: Bank of England note, 18th century. Public domain.
assets.depicts: Illustrative: an 18th-century Bank of England note, front and back; not one of Perrott's notes.

assets.credit: Thomas Morris, Ludgate Hill, London. Yale Center, CC0.
assets.depicts: An 18th-century print of shop fronts on Ludgate Street seen from Ludgate Hill, London; Perrott's own shop is not identified.

assets.credit: Henry Roberts, Newgate prison, 1781. Public domain.
assets.depicts: Newgate prison in London, shown during the Gordon riots of 1780, 19 years after Perrott; used for the prison where he was held.

assets.credit: William Hogarth, Arrested for Debt, 1735. Public domain.
assets.depicts: Illustrative: Hogarth's 1735 print of a young man arrested for debt in a London street; fiction, not a bankrupt named here.

assets.credit: William Hogarth, In the Fleet Prison, 1735. Yale, CC0.
assets.depicts: Illustrative: Hogarth's 1735 print of a debtor in the Fleet prison, London; fiction.

assets.credit: William Hogarth, a London hanging, 1747. The Met, CC0.
assets.depicts: Illustrative: Hogarth's 1747 print of a crowd at a hanging at Tyburn, London; not Perrott, and not Smithfield.
